purpose: Validate the production source-order runner and C backend with GCC AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.

execution.command_order: Run the listed commands in order. Each command inherits the environment and CPU affinity above.
execution.forced_rebuild: The first make command uses -B. It rebuilds the core, runner, seed backend, C-compiled backend, shared backend, and unit tests.

foundation_cases: Buffer overlap and growth, including the one-byte append path.
Quoted bytes compiled as C and executed.
Allocation failure reaches the required error path.
c_backend.generation_check: Seed, self, and next generations emit equal C and exact-symbol response files.

sanitizer_scope: GCC AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer instrument the C core, runner, runtime, and C-compiled RMD backend.
LeakSanitizer is disabled because its ptrace restriction fails in this execution environment.
The assembly seed compiler output and some native test fixtures are not compiler-instrumented; they execute with the sanitizer runtime.
The foundation allocation-failure subprocess adds allocator_may_return_null=1 so allocation failure reaches its required error path.
log_path_rule: Log paths are relative to the repository root. The embedded logs are durable evidence. @REPO@ replaces the absolute repository directory in log text.
